clue.text: Blows in the face

parts.note: reads like punches to the face, but means gusts of wind blowing straight against someone moving forward

explanation.surface: Someone takes punches to the face in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Winds blowing against a traveller's direction strike them full in the face.

clue.text: Reflection from one of the chosen

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows, crossing the gap between them

explanation.surface: A thought offered by one of the elect, God's chosen people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection' suggests thoughtful musing, but it is a sound bounced back; the letters straddle 'thE CHOsen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound bouncing back off a surface is a reflection of it.

clue.text: Large number cornered kept on a string, as it were

definitions.text: kept on a string, as it were

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
something cornered has been given an angle, so angled

explanation.surface: A big crowd was trapped in a corner and strung along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' marks the definition as figurative: to be dangled is to be held out like a bait on a string.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangled hangs loosely, as a puppet or bait hangs from a thread.

clue.text: Apprehension clearly visible

definitions.meaning: apprehension here is grasp or understanding of something
split as two words, something in plain view is '...'

explanation.surface: A worry that is plain for everyone to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perception or understanding, and in sight, as two words, means within view.

clue.text: … thanks to a lawman giving the facts

indicators.note: one piece is attached to the end of the other, so the thanks comes after the lawman

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American law officer
TA is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, a law officer is thanked for providing information.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue the previous clue's sentence; they play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are the gathered pieces of information, the facts on which a conclusion rests.

clue.text: Form of transport holding travellers in suspense

definitions.text: Form of transport holding travellers in suspense

parts.words: Form of transport holding travellers in suspense
parts.note: suggests a thriller that keeps passengers anxious, but means a system carrying them literally suspended high on cables

explanation.surface: A ride that keeps passengers on tenterhooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car system carries its passengers hanging in cabins above the ground.

clue.text: Fail to grasp a connection with a sewer

definitions.text: Fail to grasp a connection with a sewer

parts.words: Fail to grasp a connection with a sewer
parts.note: a person sewing who drops the yarn from the needle, read figuratively as failing to follow an argument

explanation.surface: Someone cannot see how a drain links up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain, but is someone who sews, pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop following the line of an argument is likened to a stitcher dropping their yarn.

clue.text: This came in on a change at the Industrial Revolution

definitions.text: This came in on a change at the Industrial Revolution

indicators.note: a change to the letters of the words before it reorders them into a new word

explanation.surface: Machinery arrived and transformed working life during the Industrial Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges THIS CAME IN ON A, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Industrial Revolution was the period when machines replaced hand labour in industry.

clue.text: Feline gossipers

parts.note: a tabby is an old word for a gossiping woman and a cat is a spiteful one, while both words also describe striped domestic felines

explanation.surface: Spiteful women who chatter about others.
explanation.definitionFit: Striped pet moggies share names with old slang for women given to tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Unwelcome way of projecting oneself

parts.note: describes pushing oneself forward into a place or conversation where one is not wanted

explanation.surface: Advice against pushy self-promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusting oneself forward without invitation is intrusive, sticking out where not wanted.

clue.text: A team's turning point

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football side, so the team's gives XI's

explanation.surface: A sports side reaches the moment that changes its fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning point' reads as a crisis, but is the line about which something rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning body rotates about a central line, its pivot.

clue.text: Obstructive footwear

parts.note: wooden-soled shoes whose name, as a verb, also means blocks up or chokes

explanation.surface: Shoes that get in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden shoes share a name with a verb for jamming or blocking a pipe.

clue.text: Direction to sink a pioneer Channel swimmer

parts.note: W is west, a compass direction
the tide sinks when it ebbs, so to sink is to ebb

explanation.surface: An instruction to drown an early swimmer of the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Matthew Webb was the first person recorded swimming the English Channel, in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Matthew Webb first swam from England to France unaided in 1875.

clue.text: Fanatical offer for Burlington House?

parts.note: Burlington House in London is the home of the Royal Academy, RA
a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: An extreme proposal to buy a famous London mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House on Piccadilly houses the Royal Academy of Arts, abbreviated RA; 'offer for' puts the BID after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabid supporter is extreme or zealous in their enthusiasm.

clue.text: Joint of mutton a serviceman procured

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
to have procured something is to have got it

explanation.surface: A soldier obtained a leg of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a leg of mutton or lamb, a French culinary term.

clue.text: Island post, perhaps, with about two pounds provision of-food

indicators.note: the meal-provision word goes around, or about, the pair of pounds

parts.note: board is meals provided, as in bed and board
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: An island outpost is supplied with food costing a couple of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island' is a traffic island, and the post is the short pillar on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short post marking a traffic island in the road is one example.

clue.text: There's love lost to strike a girl that way

indicators.note: the zero letter goes missing from the short word it sits in

parts.note: taken as the word to
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to strike is to hit
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A violent man heads off to hit a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' opens the clue as a link; 'lost' takes the O from TO, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb for towards that place, the opposite of hither.

clue.text: Good cup of tea left on ice

parts.note: cha is informal British for tea

explanation.surface: A fine cup of tea has been set on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins definition to wordplay, and 'on' sets the pieces side by side. 'Good' marks the cup as holy.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet used for communion wine in church services, a sacred drinking vessel.

clue.text: Point to a list of what may be taken in

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
a table is a list of figures or facts

explanation.surface: Indicating a menu of food that can be consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food fit to swallow is fit to be consumed, so edible.

clue.text: Had a swell time at the gorge?

definitions.text: Had a swell time at the gorge?

parts.words: Had a swell time at the gorge?
parts.note: reads as an enjoyable outing to a ravine, but describes a stomach puffed up after gorging on food

explanation.surface: Tourists enjoy a great visit to a canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeating leaves one swollen, so a big feed makes one puffed up.

clue.text: Sacred city a mountain god renamed Varanasi

parts.note: ben is Scottish for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A holy Indian city named after a mountain deity, later called Varanasi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renamed Varanasi' adds that this is the old name of Varanasi, the Hindu holy city on the Ganges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu pilgrimage city on the Ganges was long known by this older name.

clue.text: Sound as a bell

parts.note: the stock phrase means perfectly healthy, but read literally means to ring slowly as a bell does

explanation.surface: Something in perfect working order.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell rings out with slow, repeated strokes, as for a funeral.

clue.text: All agreed to make up for deficiencies

definitions.meaning: split as two words, people all agreed are ...
to make amends for wrongs or failings

explanation.surface: Everyone concurred on a plan to compensate for shortfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: At one, as two words, means in harmony; as one word, it means to make amends.

clue.text: A single Sussex flower

parts.note: a single is one run in cricket

explanation.surface: One bloom from a garden in Sussex, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, a river: the Arun runs through Sussex, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and this river runs through Sussex to the sea.

clue.text: Tips over a spadeful

indicators.note: turned over, the word before it is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone tips a shovel's load onto a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is the depth of earth a spade blade digs in one go.

clue.text: It's a job fixing top hose in car

indicators.note: the vehicle word has the selected letter placed in it
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A task: repairing the top of a hosepipe in a motor car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' is a link; a char is a cleaner, and to char is to do cleaning work.
explanation.definitionFit: Charring is domestic cleaning work done for pay, a cleaning lady's occupation.

clue.text: Wish when there are smiles in the maternity ward

definitions.text: Wish when there are smiles in the maternity ward

parts.words: Wish when there are smiles in the maternity ward
parts.note: a greeting usually given each year, read as celebrating the actual day of a baby's arrival

explanation.surface: Joy at a hospital where babies are born.
explanation.definitionFit: The yearly greeting marks a delivery date, and a delivery ward sees the original day.

clue.text: Somehow a result that is found taking it easy

indicators.note: in some unexplained way the letters get reshuffled

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A conclusion is somehow reached while relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unhurried and free of duties is being relaxed.
